findings.detail: The long repeats the source synopsis’s claims that Trump committed “betrayal,” sided with a foreign adversary, was compromised or sympathetic to Russia, and chose a dictator over the United States as established conclusions. The medium correctly limits the event to Trump publicly casting doubt on intelligence assessments and says there was no finding of treason or proof of an agreement.

The long reproduces the medium and supplied context nearly verbatim, including all counts, quotes and predictions. It adds no distinct context about the scope of pardons, commutations or dismissals, or their legal effect.

The long ends by saying what “this entry records” and that legal rulings and workforce tallies “require their own attribution.” Those source-management notes interrupt the otherwise useful account of the research-office closure and broader staffing changes.

The medium and long preserve an instruction to replace the previous $6.6 trillion headline, and the long discusses sources “previously attached to the event.” This is correction-history/editorial guidance rather than a reader-facing account of the two-day market decline.

The long reproduces the supplied context and medium almost verbatim, including all separation deadlines, population counts, voluntary departures and spending comparisons. It adds no explanation of the policy, the difference between diagnosis and transgender status, or the effects on service members.
